note: THE REGISTER OF WHERE THIS UNIVERSITY TEACHES FROM. One file, three readers.
It existed twice before this: as CAMPUSES in src/content/institutionalFacts.ts, which
the homepage list rendered, and as UNIVERSITY_PLACES in src/lib/flatWorld.ts, which the
map drew — plus a third bare copy of the coordinates inside scripts/build-flat-world.mjs.
Three lists of the same fact, kept in step by a comment asking somebody to remember.
That is the exact shape of a bug this repository has already shipped once: the ministry
awards moved faculty in one of two catalogues and the homepage said 'four programmes'
while the prospectus said six.
So the register is JSON, because JSON is the only format all three readers can load:
TypeScript with resolveJsonModule, and a plain node build script with JSON.parse. Adding
a place here adds it to the homepage list, to the crest's map and to the generated
flat-world.svg at once, and there is nowhere left to add it to only one of them.
WHAT MAY BE ENTERED. Only what the university has itself stated. Buea, Douala and the
Nigerian centre are on this site and in its prospectus. The United States, Zambia and
South Africa were stated by the university in August 2026, when it directed that the
homepage say 'accredited degrees taught from Cameroon, the USA, Zambia, Nigeria, South
Africa and worldwide' — and then that the campuses list and the map pins follow it.
WHAT MAY NOT. A country a student lives in. A country the fellowship reaches. A country
an alumnus serves in. A mark on a map reads as an establishment, which makes it the
easiest false claim a university website can make and the hardest for a reader to catch.
'establishment' IS THE HONEST DISTINCTION, and it is why the marks differ. Where the
university can name the site, the mark is a filled dot. Where it has named only the
nation, the mark is an open ring at the country's centre — it says 'here', not 'this
building here'. The addresses for those three are pending; see PENDING_MEASURES.
